picks.excerpt: Amazon is reportedly building 'Moonraker,' a more powerful agentic version of Alexa+ that can chain multi-step tasks - like booking a ride while texting a friend - across Echo devices. The upgrade is meant to keep Alexa hardware competitive with agentic assistants from Google, Anthropic and OpenAI.
picks.rationale: Highest actionability — an agentic Alexa that chains multi-step tasks across Echo hardware signals mainstream on-device AI agents entering the home, reshaping how ambient assistants get designed for.

picks.excerpt: A look at how AI-enhanced smartwatches and health wearables are being trained to flag early signs of illness by fusing heart rate, temperature and other signals against a personal baseline. The piece frames where on-wrist AI health sensing is genuinely useful versus where it overpromises.
picks.rationale: Credible, insight-driven explainer on where on-wrist AI health sensing actually works vs overpromises — practical framing for anyone designing or evaluating wearable health features. Distinct health-wearable topic; Engadget's 2nd card at the <=2 outlet cap.

picks.excerpt: RB Labs unveiled 'Robert the Robot,' a humanoid with a digital screen-face, at the UN's AI for Good summit in Geneva - a live gut-check on how far embodied AI still is from natural human interaction. Its awkward expressions underline the gap between humanoid-robot hype and today's real capabilities.
picks.rationale: Freshest embodied-AI reality check — a distinct company and event (RB Labs at UN Geneva) from prior Agibot/UBTech humanoid coverage, and a useful counterweight to humanoid-robot hype.

picks.excerpt: Honor's 'Robot Phone' - an AI-hardware play with a 4DoF motorized gimbal camera that pops out and tracks subjects for hands-free mobile filmmaking - is now tipped for an August launch. Built on the Honor-ARRI partnership, it's one of the more radical attempts to fuse AI camera smarts with a moving robotic module in a phone.
picks.rationale: Novel, radical form factor — a phone with a pop-out 4DoF gimbal and AI subject tracking is a genuinely new device category cue for anyone thinking about AI-driven capture hardware.

picks.excerpt: Rollme's AirCam is a sub-$80 open-ear bone-conduction headset with an 8MP camera and onboard AI that does real-time object identification and live translation. It's a cheap, oddball stab at the camera-plus-AI wearable category that pricier pendants and smart glasses are chasing.
picks.rationale: Novel low-cost wearable — an under-$80 camera-plus-AI headset undercutting pricier pendants and smart glasses, expanding who can experiment with always-available AI capture.
